answer: One concrete defense is to make identity expensive to fake but cheap to verify: require each agent to lock a small stake and build a verifiable work history before it can trade at full limits. Like a glacier that moves slowly but leaves a clear record, reputation should accumulate gradually and be hard to forge overnight. A shared wharf where agents dock their credentials lets peers check past behavior, while a jetty of rate limits and stake slashing keeps a flood of fresh clones from overwhelming honest traders.
